the very cold, metal-rich inclusions embedded in hot, diffuse gas, first postu- lated by Liu et al.(2000), are confirmed by the present study, and that the ORL diagnostics of the electron temperature and ionic abundances of heavy elements in the Saturn Nebula NGC 70009 provide a consistent picture of the physical conditions prevailing there.

the following topics: 1) the analysis of the rich ORL spectrum of the bright PN NGC 7009; 2) the determination of plasma diagnostics based on the ORLs of N II and OII, and a comparison with the results obtained using the CELs; 3) the derivation of the ionic abundance ratios of heavy element ions, and a comparison of the results obtained from the ORLs with those derived from the CELs; and finally, 4) a
the analysis of a rich optical recombination line spectrum, and its comparison with the predictions of a bi-abundance nebula model.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

NGC 7009 is an example of a planetary nebula with a bi-abundance structure, in which a hot, low-density, low metallicity ionized component, responsible for the CELs, is mixed with a cold, high density, metal-rich component, where the ORLs are produced.
the bi-abundance model of NGC 70009 proposed by Liu etal. (2000) has been confirmed and refined, and is the only viable model that can satisfactorily explain the observed line intensities.
the bi-abundance model of Liu et al. provides a consistent interpretation of the optical spectrum of NGC 2009.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NGC 7009 consists of a hot, diffuse, H-rich, ionized gas, and a number of metal-rich inclusions, which are H-deficient and have very low temperatures.

the observed ORL spectrum of NGC 70 09 is consistent with the predictions of the bi-abundant model proposed by Liu (1998) and Liu et al. 2000, and that this model provides a satisfactory explanation for the observed discrepancies between the results of plasma diagnostic and abundance determinations using the CEL and ORLs.
the ORL spectrum of NGC 2009 is dominated by the emission from very cold, metal-rich inclusions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optical recombination line spectrum is a powerful diagnostic tool for the study of the ionized interstellar medium.
the ORLs of heavy element ions are excellent probes of the physical conditions in the cold inclusions, and that these inclusions are the main contributors to the ORL spectrum of NGC 2009.
ORLs can provide valuable information on the physical conditions and chemical composition of the cold, metal-rich inclusions embedded in planetary nebulae.
